title: From Japan to the World Matcha Goes Mainstream
paragraphs: Matcha, a powdered green tea that has been used in traditional Japanese tea ceremonies for centuries, has become a global trend. Today, matcha lattes and matcha desserts can be found in cafes all over the world, and the boom is having a huge effect on Japan's tea industry.

According to data from Japan's Finance Ministry, Japan exported 13,125 tons of green tea in the fiscal year that ended in March 2026. That was 42% more than the year before. The value of these exports more than doubled to 84.7 billion yen, partly because prices rose as demand increased. Powdered green tea, including matcha, made up about 70% of the exports. The government says this is due to the popularity of matcha drinks and desserts overseas.

The trend can be seen in places like Berlin, Germany. Julia Winkels opened a matcha cafe there in 2022, and in summer, there are long lines of customers. The cafe's best-selling drink is a banana bread matcha latte. Winkels believes that matcha has now become a strong rival to coffee.

However, the boom has also caused problems. Supply has not been able to keep up with demand. In Japan, one well-known matcha ice cream was even discontinued because there was not enough matcha. Meanwhile, some products sold overseas have been fake, including some falsely labeled as coming from Uji in Kyoto, a famous tea-growing area.

Japanese tea farmers also face challenges. Many tea fields are in hilly or mountainous areas, and many farmers are getting older. Some farmers are switching from growing ordinary green tea to the leaves used for matcha, but this is expensive, and they do not know how long the boom will last.
Some people also worry about tradition. Nobuko Sugai, who leads a tea ceremony group in Berlin, said that the tradition needs to be passed on correctly.
